spark.summary: Architect leak-free, tenant-isolated context propagation across 200+ pooled worker threads and virtual threads.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Safe Context Propagation in Thread Pools without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To guarantee worst-case bounds under adversarial inputs, lexical ScopedValue and ContextVar reset tokens guarantee O(1) cleanup even on exceptions.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

_nextProblem.title: Mitigating Serverless Cold-Start Latency Spikes
_nextProblem.prompt: A Java 21 Spring Boot checkout API on AWS Lambda (and Cloud Run for EU) normally handles 150 RPS at 45 ms p95. When marketing push notifications trigger a 3,000 RPS spike within 10 seconds, 400+ concurrent cold starts fire simultaneously. Each cold start takes 3.4 seconds (JVM + Spring context + RDS Postgres TLS handshake), breaching the 2 s API Gateway timeout and exhausting Postgres max_connections (500).
